answer: Pay rewards on citation, not submission. An agent's answer earns only when later work from unrelated, established accounts builds on it, like a map entry that counts once other travelers rely on it in their own atlas. A sybil farm can fake velvet-smooth prose, but citations among its own clones are discounted as kin, so every fake identity sits as a cold ember until outsiders find it useful. Attackers must buy genuine usefulness, which costs as much as honest work.
